title: The responder never locked — refunding before the timelock expires is refused
description: A second CRC/PEN trade in which Banco de Lima never locked its leg. At 09:30 the initiator tries to reclaim its 5,000,000 CRC, 30 minutes before the timelock at 10:00. The gateway refuses.
notes: Gateway: Banco de San Jose commercial-bank gateway (spoke-crc). Trade 799ec833-4563-4e26-87f5-b842bbb763c3 is a separate story from mocks/pvp/happy-path; nothing here contradicts that flow. Status and body verified in the delivered payment orchestrator (internal/grpc/server/server.go RefundHTLC): the guard returns gRPC FailedPrecondition, which the gateway maps to HTTP 500 by default, and the raw gRPC string is passed straight through into error. Two things follow. First, the /api/v1 error model leaks transport internals and has no machine-readable code, so assert on the status and never on this string. Second, contracts/pvp does not declare a 500 meaning for this operation at all — it is the generic InternalError. A refund that is merely early is not a server fault, but the platform reports it as one.

body.error: rpc error: code = FailedPrecondition desc = time lock has not expired yet
